chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who is in a hurry, prays the Salat of Ja'far in isolation, then fulfills the glorifications while he is going regarding his needs.'

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحَ: The glorifications (recitation of phrases like SubhanAllah, etc.)
key_terms.صَلَاةَ جَعْفَرٍ: Salat of Ja'far (a specific two-rak'ah prayer with specific glorifications)
key_terms.مُجَرَّدَةً: In isolation / separately (referring to performing the prayer structure first)

ai.seo_question: How to perform Salat al-Ja'far when in a hurry?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the flexibility of the Salat al-Tasbih by permitting the separation of the prayer's structural units (rak'ahs) from the recitation of the glorifications, allowing the latter to be performed while walking or attending to daily affairs. This ruling highlights the practical ease (rukhsah) intended for the believer, ensuring that this supererogatory prayer remains accessible even during travel or busyness, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary acts of worship.
